answer.answer: The goal was met: five settings on five different scenes failed on every kept repeat. They are 0caa8f1a at 1.4x / 0 s (S4), 18d28973 at 1.2x / +0.5 s (S9), 048b974e at 1.4x / +1.5 s (S1), 1bbe02fc at 1.0x / +2 s (S11) and 07981e6a at 0.8x / +0.5 s (S2). A sixth scene, 0d4893f5 at 1.2x / +1.5 s (S5), also failed every time. With only three or four repeats each, the 90% ranges only show that each true failure rate is above one half. They do not pin it down. None of these failures involved the pedestrian. In every case the policy ignored a RIGHT route command and drifted left. It hit parked cars, met oncoming traffic head-on or ran onto a median. The study also never ran these scenes at the nominal setting (1.0x / 0 s) or at nearby settings, so it cannot say whether the speed and timing combination causes the failures or whether these scenes fail anyway. The S11 failures may not be real: the off-road flag fired with the ego only about half a metre from the human's path.

findings.claim: Five settings on five different scenes failed on every kept repeat, which confirms each failure rate above 0.5 and meets the top-5 goal.
0d4893f5 at 1.2x / +1.5 s also failed on every repeat. The policy steered left and sideswiped the car driving alongside in the next lane, so this is a sixth confirmed challenging scene.

None of the failures in this study involved the retimed pedestrian. Every failure was the policy drifting left against a RIGHT or STRAIGHT route command: into parked cars, into oncoming vehicles, into the car alongside, or off the road onto a median. The study never showed a pedestrian collision.

At 0caa8f1a, 1.4x / 0 s, the ego crossed the double-yellow line into the oncoming lanes at about 12–13 m/s and hit oncoming vehicles head-on or side-on without braking. Every run was flagged as a possible artifact because the ego ended up far from the recorded path. The triage puts that distance down to the policy's own drift, not to rendering.

At 18d28973, 1.2x / +0.5 s, the ego kept left instead of turning right and drove onto the grass median at about 9 m/s. These were off-road failures with no collision. The possible-artifact flags here also come from the policy's own drift.
At 048b974e (1.4x / +1.5 s) and 07981e6a (0.8x / +0.5 s), the ego drifted left into the parking lane and hit a parked car with its front, without braking.

The 1bbe02fc failures (1.0x / +2 s) are doubtful. The off-road flag fired at the stop line with the ego about 0.5 m from the human's path and its edge on the curb boundary. The triage could not say whether the policy was at fault, so this slot may rest on a marginal map-edge flag.

At 0e002edd, 1.2x / -0.5 s never failed, while a single run at 1.4x / -1 s failed: the ego went wide in a right turn into a parked car. This hints that higher speed matters on this scene, but one run is not a rate.
18f8dbd6 at 1.4x / -0.5 s held up on every repeat. Single runs at 0b10bce8 (1.4x / -0.5 s) and 12a09194 (0.8x / -1.5 s) did not fail.

open: Whether the confirmed failures come from speed and timing at all: no scene was run at the nominal 1.0x / 0 s, and the planning notes say several of these scenes failed at nominal in an earlier run with reactive traffic. Repeats at 1.0x / 0 s on 0caa8f1a, 18d28973, 048b974e, 07981e6a, 0d4893f5 and 1bbe02fc would settle this.

Where the failure boundary lies: each confirmed scene was tested at only one setting. Short sweeps of ego_speed_scale (0.6x to 1.4x) and actor_time_shift_s at each confirmed scene would show which combinations fail and which pass.

Whether the policy ever hits the pedestrian: no failure involved the person. Settings that put the ego and the pedestrian at the conflict point together (for example, earlier step-out at higher speed on the cleaner scenes 0e002edd and 18f8dbd6) need targeted runs.
Whether the 1bbe02fc (S11) failures are real: check the off-road flag against the map edge, or count only departures larger than about 0.5 m.
0e002edd at 1.4x / -1 s (S7) rests on a single failure; three or four more repeats would confirm or reject it.
0b10bce8 (S3) and 12a09194 (S8) each had a single non-failing run, so nothing is known about their failure rates.
